transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

They... my lieutenant sent me. I was just at the station, working with the... the airway bags. I was moving them into a pattern. It was a pattern I knew was right. I was just saying the dispatch numbers out loud to keep it straight. 

He told me to stop and step away. But I couldn't. If I broke the sequence... the whole bay would go bad. Everything would just go bad. So I didn't move. And they made me come here.
When you think about it now, do you feel that fear—that everything would go bad if you stopped the pattern—was somewhat unreasonable or exaggerated, or does it still feel like it was absolutely true?
I don't... I'm not really sure. It just... it felt like I had to finish it. I don't really know about the rest of it. That's just what was happening.

Besides this feeling about the pattern, have you noticed anything else unusual lately—like hearing voices or sounds that others don't seem to hear, or having other beliefs that people around you don't share?

I don't... I haven't heard any voices. But... I know things. I know what they're doing. 

The injury review people... and some of the supervisors. They watch me. Through the station cameras. I know they do. And... they've been going into my triage notes. Changing things. Making it look like I'm doing things wrong... like I'm unsafe. They say it's just routine paperwork when I ask, but... I know what they're doing.

How long have you noticed this feeling that people are watching you through the cameras and changing your notes—did it start recently, like in the past few weeks, or has it been going on for months or longer?
About... two months, I guess. The cameras and the paperwork. And the... the stuff at the station today. It's been about two months.
Before these last two months, did you notice any changes in yourself—like pulling away from friends or family, trouble at work, or unusual thoughts—that started earlier, even if they were milder?

I don't... I don't really know about pulling away or any of that. But... I guess it all started about eight months ago. 

I got hurt on the job. We were doing an ambulance transfer and... I messed up my shoulder. And my ribs. After that... that's just when all this started.
Since this all began, have you noticed any changes in your motivation, energy, or ability to keep up with your usual work and daily responsibilities?

I... I can't really do the ambulance anymore. They put me on desk duty, but... I don't know, the notes and the equipment checks... they said I was messing them up. So they just... they took me off the schedule. 

And at home... I just don't do much. I don't really see my friends anymore. It's just... hard to keep up with it all.
Have you noticed that your emotions feel flatter or harder to express, or that you have less interest in things you used to enjoy, since this all started?

Yeah, I guess. I just... I don't really do much anymore. Most days I just sit in my apartment. There's... there's trash in the corner, food just sitting in the fridge. I don't really cook anymore. I used to play basketball with the guys, but... I don't call them. I just... I can't get myself to care. Or start anything. It's just... flat, I guess.
Do you ever notice that your thoughts feel jumbled or hard to organize, or that you have trouble following a conversation or expressing your thoughts clearly to others?
I don't... I don't think so. I can follow what you're saying fine. I just... I don't really talk to people much anyway. So... no, not really.
During these past several months, have you had any stretches where your mood was noticeably low, hopeless, or overly high and energetic, separate from what you've already described?
No, not really. Just... what I already said. I don't get high and energetic. I just sit there.
